title: Concise Response — prototype journal
content:
Notes to self / experiment journal for a small feature: 'concise responses' (user-controlled brevity)

Background:
- Problem: users complain about verbose assistants in low-cost or mobile contexts. We lose tokens and latency increases. Need a lightweight UX + server-side policy to bias models toward shorter outputs without major quality regressions.
- Goal: provide a simple user-facing toggle + implicit heuristics that reduce average token output 20–50% for targeted flows (summarization, FAQs, chat brief mode).

Hypotheses:
1) A short explicit control (slider/toggle: "Concise / Normal") reduces output length by ~30% on query set while preserving >=90% task success (measured by human eval).
2) Combining a concise prefix + lower temperature + response-length penalty at sampling yields better tradeoffs than just max_tokens cap.
3) Telemetry + lightweight automatic quality checks (BLEU-ish + semantic-closeness embeddings) can catch major regressions fast; manual evals required for edge cases.

User stories:
- As a mobile user, I want shorter replies when on metered data so I get necessary info quickly and pay less.
- As a support agent, I want a "brief mode" to generate short canned responses to speed triage.
- As an admin, I want to enforce concise defaults for a given route to control cost for high-volume endpoints.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- UI: toggle in client SDK + REST param concise=true (and concise_level: low|med|high optional).
- Server: route-level policy can default concise true/false.
- Sampling knobs: implicit instruction template + sampling penalties applied when concise=true.
- Metrics: track median tokens, 95th percentile latency, human-quality score baseline comparison.
- Rollout: canary to 5% traffic; automatic rollback on X% quality regression or Y% error increase.

Design ideas / implementation sketches:
- Client: small toggle in Playground + SDK param. concise_level map: low ~ 10% shorter, med ~ 30%, high ~ 50% target.
- Prompt template: prepend system instruction like: "Be concise: prefer single-sentence answers unless user asks for elaboration. If multiple steps required, give a 1-2 line summary and then offer 'more details?'\."
- Sampling: reduce top_k? prefer nucleus smaller (p=0.8 -> 0.6), add length_penalty -0.8, reduce temperature by 0.2.
- Max token cap: avoid hard cap because it truncates important content; use soft penalties + greedy reranking to favor shorter outputs that meet intents.

Evaluation plan:
- Build a balanced eval set: 400 queries across categories (FAQ, stepwise instructions, creative, code snippets, clarifying Qs).
- Metrics: tokens per response, human rating (3-level: good/acceptable/bad), semantic similarity (embedding cosine to reference).
- Automatic gating: if human_accept_rate < 0.9 or semantic_similarity drops by > 0.12 vs baseline, block rollout.

Telemetry / instrumentation:
- Logs: concise flag, concise_level, model, sampling params, output token count, latency, error flags.
- Alerting: weekly drift dashboard; immediate alert on sudden drop in quality for any major route.

Edge cases and risks: 
- Long-form tasks (stories, legal text): concise mode can catastrophically damage output. Need route-level opt-out and model-level detection (if prompt indicates 'detailed' requested, ignore concise).
- Safety: brevity might remove necessary safety disclaimers. Add explicit safety check that responses failing safety filters must expand or fallback to normal generation.
- Cost vs quality tradeoffs require human review per-customer; provide per-customer conservative defaults.

Prototype experiments to run (week-by-week):
- Week 1: client param + simple prompt prefix experiment (concise=yes) on a small gaggle of routes (FAQ, help bot). Collect tokens and automated similarity.
- Week 2: add sampling tweaks + level param; start human eval panels for med/high modes.
- Week 3: route-level defaulting + canary rollout; monitor metrics and safety regressions.
- Week 4: analyze results and prepare playbook for Dedicated/Private (allow customer overrides, SDK docs).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Which models to prioritize? Start with 2 midsize models that are cheapest in catalog. Need infra sign-off for telemetry delta.
- UX: concise slider vs quick presets? (ask UX for A/B)
- How to represent cost savings in Console? per-route token delta estimate?
- Internal flagging: add metadata to logs so we can filter concise traffic in billing and audits.

Quick example prompts / baseline vs concise output (notes):
- Q: "How do I reset my password?"
  baseline: 5–7 short sentences step-by-step.
  concise (med): "Go to Settings > Security > Reset password. Check email for code and follow link. Reply 'I didn't get it' if stuck."
- Q: "Explain blockchain consensus" (should detect long-form -> opt-out).

Notes to self: keep this lightweight — stakeholders want a tangible small win before full PRD. Focus on FAQ/help bot first where conciseness is high signal.

Link to quick mock: https://www.figma.com/file/concise-mock (placeholder)

End journal entry — will update after week 1 experiment results.
